primary.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
primary.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.7576 and the house-rule point is 0.7576. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

published_interval.restated_2026_08_20: The published interval is now REML, so this block compares a REML point interval against a REML Hartung-Knapp one and the ESTIMATOR is no longer one of the things that differ between them. At k=2 the moment estimator and REML coincide exactly, so not one digit of this block's numbers moved -- only the label, which was wrong.

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-20. The rule WAS decided, in DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, and applied on 2026-08-20: REML is the estimator corpus-wide, and Hartung-Knapp is a SENSITIVITY analysis at k<=3 rather than the primary interval (Handbook 6.5 s10.10.4.4-10.10.4.5). Both intervals still stand on this page and nothing is unpublished.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

A_SEPARATE_FINDING_NOT_RESOLVED_HERE_202.what: The pool combines ODDS RATIOS on a TIME-TO-FIRST-EVENT endpoint, over trials of different duration.
A_SEPARATE_FINDING_NOT_RESOLVED_HERE_202.detail: Both trials registered time to first event. This object stores odds ratios derived from cumulative arm counts, and the two trials did not run for the same length of time. AN ODDS RATIO OVER UNEQUAL FOLLOW-UP IS NOT A HAZARD RATIO AND DOES NOT BECOME ONE BY BEING POOLED: it depends on how long each trial ran, so the weights mean something different from what a reader will assume. The two trials' own published hazard ratios exist and would be the right inputs.
A_SEPARATE_FINDING_NOT_RESOLVED_HERE_202.why_it_is_recorded_and_not_fixed: Recomputing this pool from hazard ratios is a published-number change and would have to reach the heterogeneity, the estimator, the GRADE domains and the result card in one pass, per P19. Establishing the estimand and repairing the provenance labels is this pass. The two findings are independent: the endpoint IS shared, which is what this pass establishes, and the SUMMARY MEASURE may still be the wrong one, which is what this note records.
A_SEPARATE_FINDING_NOT_RESOLVED_HERE_202.what_would_settle_it: The published hazard ratios for both trials with their confidence intervals, and a decision about whether this review pools the effect measure the trials reported or the one its extractor could compute.

display_change_announced.why: A reader recomputing Higgins I-squared from the Q printed beside it would have concluded the object was wrong -- and would have been behaving exactly as we want readers to behave. An ambiguous label on an unambiguous number is a defect specifically against the only reader we claim to serve.

display_change_announced.change: estimator changed to REML -- LABEL ONLY, no value moved
display_change_announced.what_changed: This pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. It is refitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The old fit was reproduced against the stored value FIRST (REPRODUCED) and only then replaced. Stored values are also rounded at storage -- effects to 4 decimals, tau-squared and Q to 6, I-squared to 4 -- because several of these pools carried sixteen significant figures on a two- or three-study pool.
display_change_announced.why: The corpus held two estimator conventions at once: 23 pools REML, 9 DerSimonian-Laird, 1 Paule-Mandel. Handbook 6.5 s10.10.4.4 records REML as RevMan's own current default and this project's statistics rules already refused DerSimonian-Laird below k=10, which every pool in this corpus is. The decision was taken on 2026-08-18 and not applied; applying it to some pools and not others would have been worse than either convention.

question_change_record_2026_08_20.why_it_was_wrong: It asserted that the two trials' registered primaries DIFFER. They differ by the word 'the'. The sentence was generated rather than read, and it made this pool look incoherent when it is sound.
question_change_record_2026_08_20.why_this_direction_matters: Every other defect found in this corpus this week made a page look BETTER than it was. This one made it look worse, and would have led someone to withdraw a good estimate. It survived precisely because of its direction: nobody audits a page for being too hard on itself.
